source_text: Ambulabo inter vos; ero Deus vester. Inhabitatio Dei. Templum Spiritus.
thought_title: God's indwelling presence among the faithful
orientation: Origen is applying the blessings promised in Leviticus to the spiritual life of the believer, moving from peace and victory to the promise of God's abiding presence.
pass_a_gloss: I will walk among you; I will be your God. The indwelling of God. The temple of the Spirit.

choices.why: Keeps the future tense and the physical metaphor of walking, which conveys God's ongoing, active presence with his people.
rejected: I shall walk in your midst
I will go about among you

choices.why: Preserves the covenant formula exactly, with the possessive 'vester' rendered as 'your'.
rejected: I shall be God to you
I will be a God for you

choices.why: Renders the abstract noun as a noun phrase, matching the source's compact theological statement.
Keeps the genitive 'Spiritus' as 'of the Spirit', preserving the Pauline echo of the believer as God's temple.

bible_refs.note: Ambulabo inter vos; ero Deus vester

pass_b_english: "I will walk among you, and I will be your God" (Leviticus 26:12). The indwelling of God. The temple of the Spirit.
